First-reader concern, 'whose screen is it, and how does it connect to Ravi?': acceptable. In review/page-06.png panel 1 shows the laptop bezel and camera dot, the same window and plant at the upper right, and the desk. Ananya's hand rests on the trackpad, with her white coat cuff and teal sleeve visible. It is her laptop in the same consultation, carried on from 05-4.

First-reader concern, 'dentist, eye and paediatric tools have nothing to do with tiredness': acceptable. The header 'SPECIALITY-SPECIFIC' frames the tiles as examples of how the planner adapts to each speciality, not as Ravi's diagnosis. The user asked for exactly this feature and these three examples (Request 3), and the source tells the comic to avoid treatment specifics.

First-reader concern, 'the Eye doctor and Paediatrician boxes nearly touch': this is in the preview too, about 7 px apart, so it is not a placeholder artefact. It is acceptable. Each box has its own border and sits under its own tile art (eye diagram, growth chart), and the reading order follows the tiles left to right. The Paediatrician box runs slightly below the screen onto the bezel but covers no tile art or hand.

First-reader concern, 'Ravi gives no reply': acceptable. In the preview Ravi smiles with his hands on his knees and his bag beside the chair, facing Ananya. His silent agreement is visible, and the label below is read as screen information, not a skipped reply.
In the preview, the tail on Ananya's balloon goes to her mouth. The PLAN OF CARE label sits over the laptop screen at lower left and does not cover either face or Ananya's open-hand gesture.

transitions.observation: 05-4 shows Ananya listening at the desk with the laptop open at the desk edge. The page turns to a close-up of that laptop, with the same window and plant and her hand on the trackpad, so it is the same moment in the same consultation. No time caption is needed.

The camera pulls back from the planner close-up to the two-shot past the same laptop, which now shows the plan-of-care cards, while Ananya sums up. The screen content moves forward in the order the user asked for.

Ravi's bag is on the floor beside his chair in 06-2. In review/page-07.png it is back on his shoulder at the reception desk: a monitor, a plant and waiting chairs with patients seen from behind are visible. The art establishes the move from the consultation room back to reception without a caption.

readingReview.comparison: The first reader's order (header, three tiles left to right, balloon, then the PLAN OF CARE label) agrees exactly with the script order. Nothing was skipped. Their four concerns came from grey-box placeholders: no visible owner of the screen, relevance of the specialities, nearly touching boxes, and Ravi's silence. The accepted art in review/page-06.png resolves each one, as explained above. The near-touching tile labels are also in the preview and are acceptable because the tile borders and art keep them distinct.
